prompt: What two buildings can be said to have introduced the onset of the architectural style of Big Ben in London?
answer: Big Ben is an example of **Gothic Revival (Neo-Gothic)** architecture. In London, the style is commonly associated with—and was strongly established by—**Westminster Abbey** and the **Palace of Westminster (the Houses of Parliament)**, of which Elizabeth Tower is a part.
